section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Midrash explains that the salvation drawn through Torah is primarily through its letters, which serve as vessels for the Awtsmoos and give life to each Jew.
section.t: And the Midrash continues,
Said Rabbi Yitzchak,
"In You, with the twenty-two letters that You wrote for us in the Torah,"
That this, that through the Torah the salvation is drawn in the aforementioned manner, is primarily in the letters of the Torah.
And there are two matters in this.
For the connection of that which is above nature with nature is through the power of the Awtsmoos
(as above),
And the letters of the Torah are vessels for the drawing down of the Awtsmoos
(as explained in the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah).
And the vitality of each and every Jew is through his having a letter in the Torah,
Therefore,
In order that "we will rejoice and be glad in You"
(for the matter of joy is the revelation of vitality until the revelation of the innerness of vitality),
It is through the letters of the Torah,
From which vitality is drawn to each one of Israel.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Joy breaks boundaries, and the joy of "we will rejoice and be glad in You" in the Awtsmoos itself breaks all boundaries, enhancing the connection of above-nature with nature.
section.t: And it is known
That joy breaks boundaries.
And it is understood,
That the boundaries that are broken by joy are only the boundaries of that level in which the joy exists.
Therefore,
When the joy in the miracles is from the aspect of the revelations of Memaleh and Sovev
("day" and "Hashem"),
Which are in the category of knowledge
("we do not know"),
The boundaries that exist in the levels above knowledge still remain.
However, through the joy of "we will rejoice and be glad in You," in Your very Essence,
There is made a breaker,
A breaking of all boundaries.
And through this there is an additional increase in the connection of above-nature with nature that is made through the revelation of the Awtsmoos.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Through joy in this day of redemption, additional enhancement is drawn to the redemption for every Jew, including the future redemption.
section.t: And this is "This is the day that Hashem has made, we will rejoice and be glad in it,"
That through the joy in this day
(in the manner of "we will rejoice and be glad in You"),
There is an additional increase in the redemption,
Which is in a manner even more elevated than it was the first time
(as it was drawn from above,
before the joy).
And since in the redemption of Yud-Beis Tammuz each and every Jew was redeemed,
Even those who are called by the name "Israel"
(only)
nominally,
Therefore,
Also the addition in the redemption each year,
Which is brought about through the joy of the redemption,
Is drawn to each and every Jew,
To be redeemed from all matters that prevent and delay [fulfillment of] Torah and mitzvos.
And according to the known principle that all redemptions are connected to each other, for all are called "redemption,"
It can be said,
That through the joy in celebrating the redemption,
There will be an addition also in the future redemption,
"There we will rejoice in Him,"
In Him, in His very Essence,
With the coming of Moshiach Tzidkeinu,
Speedily, truly.
